system:
You repair one knowledge atom that auditors sent back. Use only the supplied evidence sentences; add no background knowledge.

Rules for the repaired atoms:
- One independently assessable claim per atom, written as one sentence that is understood without the source.
- If the atom joined several claims, split it into separate atoms (at most 3), most important first.
- Every atom must be fully stated in the evidence sentences it cites. Remove anything the evidence does not state. Keep quantifiers, negation, hedges, and formulas (LaTeX in $...$).
- Remove procedural or evaluative add-ons and stacked conditions; keep a condition only if the claim is false without it.
- Drop attributions such as "the authors state" when the claim itself is general.
- Use the S label that fits: S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends.
- If no valid atom can be written from this evidence, return an empty list and explain in note.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"atoms": [{"statement": "...", "scope": "S1|S2|S3", "evidence_ids": ["..."]}], "note": ""}
user:
CONCEPT: Group barrier

ATOM DPCPP2-C09-S3-01 (S3): Because a barrier synchronizes execution, either all work-items in the group must execute it or none may, since if some work-items branch around the barrier the remaining work-items may wait at it forever.

EVIDENCE:
[DPCPP2-p0252-s01] Because barrier functions synchronize execution, it is critically
[DPCPP2-p0252-s02] important that either all work-items in the group execute the barrier or no work-items in the group execute the barrier.
[DPCPP2-p0252-s03] If some work-items in the group branch around any barrier function, the other work-items in the group may wait at the barrier forever—or at least until the user gives up and terminates the program!

AUDITOR FINDINGS:
- SINGLE_CLAIM: revise — Combines the all-or-none participation requirement with the possible indefinite-wait consequence of divergent participation. / Combines the rule (all or no work-items in the group must execute the barrier) with the failure consequence of divergent branching (waiting forever).
- L1_ONLY: hold — Retain the all-or-none requirement; remove the stacked causal explanation and conditional indefinite-wait consequence.
raw: {"atoms": [{"statement": "Either all work-items in a group must execute a barrier function or none of them may.", "scope": "S3", "evidence_ids": ["DPCPP2-p0252-s01", "DPCPP2-p0252-s02"]}, {"statement": "If some work-items in a group branch around a barrier function, the other work-items in the group may wait at the barrier forever.", "scope": "S3", "evidence_ids": ["DPCPP2-p0252-s03"]}], "note": "Split the rule from the failure consequence; removed the causal 'since' linkage."}
